title: A quiet week, a few flakes late, and one model dreaming big
summary: All six locations stay dry through Wednesday as this week's storm heads to California. Weak systems from Thursday to Monday bring snow levels down and a chance of an inch or two, best at Banff Sunshine and Whistler. One model, the GFS, keeps showing a big Washington storm around Oct 26–28; nothing else agrees yet.
short_term: Saturday through Wednesday (Oct 17–21): high pressure and a split flow keep the Northwest dry. A front this morning brought a few showers to the Cascades but no snow worth measuring, and snow levels sit high at 7,000–9,600 ft in Washington and 4,750–8,750 ft in Canada. Expect frosty mornings, mild afternoons and breezy ridgetops today (gusts 30–35 mph at Crystal and Whistler), easing Sunday. Every model and every ensemble member keeps the next five days essentially snow-free.
extended: Thursday through Monday (Oct 22–26): a weak, splitting system arrives Thursday and the pattern turns cooler and more unsettled. Snow levels fall to about 4,000–5,000 ft in the Cascades and as low as 2,500–3,500 ft in BC by the weekend. Amounts look light. Consensus totals are 0.1–1.1 in, and the chance of at least an inch ranges from 12% at Snoqualmie to 71% at Sunshine. The wildcard is the GFS, which builds a major storm Oct 26–28 with about 50 in at Crystal, 32 in at Snoqualmie and 23 in at Rainy Pass by Oct 31. ECMWF shows 1–4 in over the same span, and the ensembles put Crystal's 15-day median at 1.9 in. Until other guidance moves toward it, treat it as an outlier.
best_bets:
1. Banff Sunshine, Friday, Oct 23: about an inch, the most reliable chance on the board.
2. Whistler upper mountain, Monday night, Oct 26: light snow above 3,000 ft, with a long tail if the pattern trends wetter.
3. Washington: nothing worth planning around yet. Check back if the GFS storm starts to show up in ECMWF.
